transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-04-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Harvestly - Head of ML), Tom Becker (Harvestly - Platform Eng Manager), Priya Nair (Harvestly - Procurement)

Auto-summary: short check-in to align on renewal cadence and scope for an extended retainer, confirm EU and APAC activation, and decide on Dedicated trial vs Hosted ingestion. Action items captured below.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity uplift (~250k tokens/day), latency targets (p95 < 220ms), region residency (EU, APAC), compliance (SOC2/ISO, KMS), benchmark plan, contract amendment timeline.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we set 50 minutes. Quick intro from our side, Carlos is here to cover the bench and infra questions.
[00:18] Aisha (Harvestly): Thanks, yes, we've been on Redwood for 10 months, current retainer is 80k tokens/day, we expect to double to start and potentially go further. Main ask is EU region for latency and APAC pilot for a subset of traffic.
[00:35] Tom: And from platform we care about egress patterns, VPC connectivity, and whether Dedicated gives us guaranteed throughput during peak.
[00:48] Carlos (Redwood SE): Right, Dedicated is what customers pick for predictable throughput — reserved GPU pools, autoscale rules. We can run a short throughput sim to mirror your prefix cache behavior.
[01:05] Priya (Procurement): Timeline: procurement wants contract amendment in two weeks, internal budget approval end of month.
[01:20] Maya: Ok makes sense. Quick q to ground truth — what's your current p95 production latency and cost sensitivity?
[01:30] Aisha: p95 around 280ms now, some spikes at EMEA evenings. Cost sensitivity moderate — we want to keep unit cost reasonable but not at expense of user latency.
[01:45] Tom: Also: data residency needs — logs for EU traffic must stay in EU, and we need KMS integration for encryption at rest.
[02:02] Carlos: We support customer-managed KMS and can configure per-region log buckets; audit logs are available via Console or S3 export.
[02:15] Aisha: Can you confirm the difference in cost between Hosted and Dedicated? I get that dedicated is commit-based but curious about break-even.
[02:29] Maya: I'll share a side-by-side — short version: Dedicated lowers per-token CPU/GPU unit cost at scale but has a monthly reserved footprint. Hosted is OPEX-style, no commit. We'll put numbers to the 250k/day profile.
[02:45] Tom: For the APAC pilot, would you run the model in a separate geocluster? We want isolation for a pilot subset due to compliance.
[02:57] Carlos: Yep, we can route by region policy, or create a dedicated geocluster in APAC for the pilot. Fallback policy can spill to Hosted if capacity gaps occur. Note: small speech glitch in the docs — the product name is Redwood Dedicated but internal notes show 'Redwood Dedicate' sometimes — ignore that in doc export.
[03:20] Priya: On procurement flow, we need SOC2 attestation and ISO certs — can you share?
[03:28] Maya: Absolutely, I'll attach SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 summary and our DPA. Also will include sample SLA language for dedicated pools.
[03:40] Aisha: One more technical item — KV cache behavior. Our use uses long prefixes, so KV cache hit rate matters. Would the Dedicated runtime help?
[03:53] Carlos: Yes Dedicated lets you pin model variants and we can tune KV cache allocation per pool. Also continuous batching settings differ by pool size — we'll propose configs after we see your token distribution.
[04:10] Tom: Ok, show of hands — are we leaning Dedicated trial first or Hosted with region pinning?
[04:18] Aisha: Prefer to pilot Dedicated in EU for a month then decide on APAC.
[04:24] Maya: Proposed plan: 2-week Dedicated trial for EU (small reserved pool), benchmark week with SE + Harvestly infra, then contract amendment to extend retainer with staged APAC activation.
[04:37] Priya: Procurement needs estimated spend for amendment.
[04:41] Maya: I'll put a draft amendment with pricing bands: 3 tiers (hosted scale, dedicated small pool, dedicated committed) and expected MRR delta.

[06:10] (discussion pivot — Carlos goes into benchmark specifics)
[06:10] Carlos: For the benchmark we want: 1) sample prompt set and token histogram, 2) expected concurrency and p95 target, 3) KV cache patterns (prefix lengths), 4) auth flow for VPC egress test. We'll run both per-token microbench and end-to-end inference sim.
[06:35] Tom: I'll set up a small S3 bucket and share sample CSV with prompts; we'd prefer scrubbed data. Any concern about sending sample prompts?
[06:45] Carlos: Ideally scrubbed, yes. If anything sensitive, send hashed or anonymized variants. We also can run an agentless sim if needed.

[09:00] (transcription has a short mis-hear)
[09:00] Aisha: ...so the KV cash — sorry cache — tends to grow in the evenings, it's the reason we sometimes overflow.
[09:07] Carlos: totally, we saw that pattern in similar retail workloads. We'll model that.

[12:40] (pricing conversation)
[12:40] Maya: Baseline numbers I'm thinking to share: hosted at current usage cost X, dedicated small pool at commit Y with expected 18% unit cost reduction at 250k tokens/day, committed large pool shows ~34% reduction. Numbers will be in the sheet.
[13:05] Priya: Will discounts be upfront or monthly?
[13:10] Maya: For committed we do monthly credit against the retainer, with annual/quarterly billing options. We'll note payment terms in amendment.

[18:20] (compliance + legal Q&A)
[18:20] Priya: Data retention: can we set retention policy for logs to 90 days for EU?
[18:28] Carlos: Yes, you can configure retention per log export and we can set log export to your EU S3 with lifecycle rules.
[18:35] Aisha: Audit logs — do they capture token-level request traces or just request IDs? We need enough to debug but not PII.
[18:45] Carlos: We redact PII by default and logs contain request metadata, model version, route, and timing. Full payload only available if customer opts in and we recommend hashed or masked payloads for regulated data.

[25:10] (discussion around failover and fallback)
[25:10] Tom: If dedicated pool saturates, will routing fallback cause latency spike?
[25:20] Carlos: We have policy-based fallback; traffic can spill to Hosted and we can set percent thresholds. For critical endpoints we recommend canary routing and reserve burst capacity.

[31:45] (questions about metrics & console)
[31:45] Maya: Console provides token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, model KPIs, and alerting. Can push webhooks to your PagerDuty.
[32:00] Aisha: Great — we want a dashboard showing p95 and cost per route.
[32:05] Carlos: We'll include a dashboard template in the readout.

[38:00] (bench plan recap)
[38:00] Maya: To be explicit: harvestly provides sample prompts by Apr 10; Carlos + Tom to run bench and deliver results by Apr 15; Maya will draft amendment by Apr 8; then a week-of-Apr20 bench deep-dive session.
[38:16] Priya: That timeline works for procurement conditional on the amendment doc.

[45:50] (closing questions and recap)
[45:50] Aisha: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[45:56] Maya: None, just need your sample data and signoff to kick the trial. We'll include a short MSA addendum for the dedicated trial.
[46:10] Tom: Clarify: for the APAC pilot, do we need a separate Egress IP allow-list?
[46:16] Carlos: We can provide static egress IP ranges per geocluster; we'll share the list prior to pilot activation.
[46:30] Maya: Ok I'll send the follow-up email with links. Links/resources: link to SOC2/ISO: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack, dedicated pricing draft: https://redwood.example.com/harvestly/pricing-draft, bench-runner repo (internal): https://git.internal/redwood/bench-runner (read-only).

[51:00] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email; action items in the doc.
[51:05] End of recording.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — a few SS transcription errors ('KV cash' for cache, 'Redwood Dedicate' mislabel)
